He earned a gold medal with [[USA Basketball]] at the [[2014 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]]. A prospective target of many [[college basketball]] recruiters, he committed to the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]] in May 2015, but reopened his recruitment and committed to [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]]. ==Early life== A native of [[Edison, New Jersey]],Waters, Mike. [http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2015/11/why_syracuse_recruit_tyus_battle_switched_schools_high_schools_that_is.html 'Why Syracuse recruit Tyus Battle switched schools ... high schools, that is"], [[The Post-Standard]], November 13, 2015. Accessed February 2, 2017. "Battle lives in Edison, N.J., with his father, brother, sister and step-mother. His mother, Daniella Battle, lives nearby. Gill St. Bernards is located in Gladstone, N.J. It's about a 30-minute drive north into Somerset County."{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2461055-tyus-battle-to-michigan-wolverines-land-5-star-sg-prospect|title=Tyus Battle to Michigan: Wolverines Land 5-Star SG Prospect|access-date=May 12, 2015|date=May 11, 2015|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|author=Chiari, Mike}} Battle first became a nationally ranked basketball player in sixth grade.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/08/03/magazine/in-search-of-the-next-andrew-wiggins.html?_r=0|title=In Search of the Next Andrew Wiggins|access-date=May 12, 2015|date=July 30, 2014|work=[[The New York Times]]|author=Wiedeman, Reeves}} He played for [[Gill St. Bernard's School]] in [[Gladstone, New Jersey]] for freshman, sophomore, and junior year but then transferred to [[St. Joseph High School (Metuchen, New Jersey)|St. Joseph High School]] in [[Metuchen, New Jersey]], which was closer to home and allowed him to follow in the footsteps of former standouts of the school [[Jay Williams (basketball)|Jay Williams]] and [[Karl-Anthony Towns]]. Battle earned high rankings among the national class of 2016. Although he endured a wrist injury during the season,{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.nj.com/news/article/-3333891458817276277/boys-basketball-with-tyus-battle-sidelined-gill-st-bernards-battles-against-st-peters/|title=Boys Basketball: With Tyus Battle sidelined, Gill St. Bernard's battles against St. Peter's|access-date=May 12, 2015|date=February 3, 2014|website=[[NJ.com]]|author=Schneider, Jeremy}} Battle had averaged 22.5 [[point (basketball)|points]], 6.3 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], 3.6 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] and 2 [[steal (basketball)|steals]] per game as a 2013–14 sophomore. As a junior, Battle missed the first six weeks of the season with a foot injury after being named the [[Somerset County, New Jersey]] player of the year as a sophomore. He returned to the lineup at the end of January 2015.{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.nj.com/news/article/-4798120771239063101/boys-basketball-tyus-battle-to-make-season-debut-for-gill-st-bernards-on-saturday-against-ridge/|title=Boys Basketball: Tyus Battle to make season debut for Gill St. Bernard's on Saturday against Ridge|access-date=May 12, 2015|date=January 30, 2015|website=[[NJ.com]]|author=Schneider, Jeremy}} He only appeared in 9 games during his junior season, as a result.{{cite web|url=http://highschoolsports.nj.com/news/article/-6145999196322224454/boys-basketball-gill-st-bernards-tyus-battle-commits-to-michigan/|title=Boys Basketball: Gill St. Bernard's guard Tyus Battle commits to Michigan|access-date=May 12, 2015|date=May 11, 2015|website=[[NJ.com]]|author=Schneider, Jeremy}} His average fell to 16.9 points in his limited junior campaign. Michigan made Battle a scholarship offer in June 2014.{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2014/07/michigan_basketball_recruiting.html|title=Michigan target Tyus Battle lands on U.S. U17 team, other basketball recruiting notes|access-date=May 12, 2015|date=July 31, 2014|website=[[MLive.com]]|author=Quinn, Brendan F.}} [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] [[head coach]] [[John Calipari]] visited Battle on Halloween 2014. After receiving 24 scholarship offers, Battle narrowed his list of schools to 11 on November 3, 2014, via Twitter: [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]], [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]], [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], Kentucky, [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]], [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], and Michigan.{{cite recruiting|access-date=May 12, 2015|date=November 3, 2014|publisher=[[Cleveland.com]]|author=Landis, Bill}} He narrowed his list of candidate schools to seven on February 23, 2015: Connecticut, web|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/02/23/five-star-class-2016-shooting-guard-tyus-battle-cuts-list-seven-duke-louisville-michigan-notre-dame-ohio-state-syracuse-uconn/|title= web|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2015/05/report_2016_recruiting_target_tyus_battle_schedules_official_visit_to_syracuse.html|title=2016 recruiting target Tyus Battle schedules official visit to Syracuse|access-date=May 12, 2015|date=May 5, 2015|publisher=[[Syracuse.com]]|author=Waters, Mike}} Syracuse coach [[Jim Boeheim]] had an in-home visit with Battle. Battle had also visited a Michigan camp during the summer of 2014. At the time of his May 11, 2015 verbal commitment, he ranked {{Abbr|no.|number}} 14 as a 5-star member of the [[ESPN]] 60 for the class of 2016.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/12866568/tyus-battle-2016-five-star-guard-commits-michigan-wolverines|title=Tyus Battle commits to Michigan|access-date=May 12, 2015|date=May 11, 2015|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Borzello, Jeff}} He was also ranked no. 14 by [[Rivals.com]],{{cite web|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/05/11/michigan-lands-commitment-from-top-15-recruit-tyus-battle/|title=Michigan lands commitment from top 15 recruit Tyus Battle|access-date=May 12, 2015|date=May 11, 2015|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|author=Dauser, Rob}} no. 10 by [[Scout.com]],{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/story/1545577-battle-gives-early-commitment|title=Tyus Battle Commits To Michigan|access-date=May 12, 2015|date=May 11, 2015|publisher=[[Scout.com]]|author=Daniels, Evan}} and no. 12 by [[247Sports.com]].{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25181343/michigan-lands-2016-five-star-talent-tyus-battle|title=Michigan lands 2016 five-star talent Tyus Battle|access-date=May 12, 2015|date=May 11, 2015|work=[[CBS Sports]]|author=Norlander, Matt}} He was the no. 4 shooting guard in the class according to 247Sports. Battle had taken his official visit at Michigan on May 7.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2015-05-11/tyus-battle-commits-to-michigan-wolverines-class-of-2016-five-star-recruit|title=Five-star guard Tyus Battle commits to Michigan|access-date=May 12, 2015|date=May 11, 2015|work=[[Sporting News]]|author=Thomas, Colleen}} At the time of his signing, Michigan had the top 2016 recruiting class with Battle and a pair of {{convert|6|ft|10|in|m|2}} [[center (basketball)|center]]s ([[Jon Teske]] and Austin Davis).{{cite web|url=http://den.247sports.com/Bolt/Wolverines-Currently-Have-Top-2016-Class-37221434|title=Wolverines Currently Have Top 2016 Class|access-date=May 12, 2015|date=May 11, 2015|publisher=[[247Sports.com]]|author=Lorenz, Steve}}{{dead link|date=April 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Although at the time of Battle's signing, the entire set of scholarships for the class of 2016 seemed to be allocated,{{cite web|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2015/05/11/michigan-basketball-tyus-battle/27127035/|title=U-M gets commitment from 5-star guard Tyus Battle|access-date=May 12, 2015|date=May 11, 2015|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|author=Manzullo, Brian and By Perry A. Farrell}} some sources reported that Michigan was expected to continue to lure point guards like [[Cassius Winston]] and Devearl Ramsey to play with Battle. 2018|publisher=[[NCAA]]|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}} As a sophomore, Tyus Battle scored his 1,000th point. He averaged 19.2 points per game on 32 percent shooting from the 3-point line. Following his sophomore season, Battle declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] without signing with an agent.{{cite news|last1=Ditota|first1=Donna|title=Tyus Battle declares for NBA Draft, won't hire an agent|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2018/04/tyus_battle_syracuse_basketball_nba_draft.html|access-date=April 22, 2018|work=[[Syracuse.com]]|date=April 20, 2018}} On May 30, 2018, Battle withdrew his name from the draft to return to Syracuse for his junior season.{{cite news|last1=Goodman|first1=Jeff|title=Tyus Battle to play junior season at Syracuse|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23653112/tyus-battle-returning-syracuse-orange-dropping-nba-draft|access-date=May 30, 2018|work=[[espn.com]]|date=May 30, 2018}} He averaged 17.2 points per game as a junior and improved his shooting. At the end of the season he declared for the NBA draft, forfeiting his final season of eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Waters |first1=Mike |title=Syracuse's Tyus Battle enters 2019 NBA draft more mature, more prepared |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2019/06/syracuses-tyus-battle-enters-2019-nba-draft-more-mature-more-prepared.html |access-date=November 26, 2019 |work=[[Syracuse.com]] |date=June 7, 2019}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]], Battle signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2019/06/former-syracuse-star-tyus-battle-will-reportedly-sign-with-minnesota-timberwolves.html|title=Former Syracuse star Tyus Battle will reportedly sign with Minnesota Timberwolves|access-date=July 1, 2019|date=June 21, 2019|website=[[Syracuse.com]]|author=Carlson, Chris}} He was officially added to the Timberwolves’ preseason roster on October 14.{{cite news |title=Timberwolves sign Tyus Battle and Barry Brown Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-tyus-battle-and-barry-brown-jr |access-date=October 19, 2019 |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=October 14, 2019}} He was released and added to the Timberwolves’ [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Iowa Wolves]].{{cite news |last1=Lawhon |first1=Danny |title=New energy and a familiar face bring Iowa Wolves into 2019-20 NBA G League season |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/basketball/iowa-wolves/2019/11/07/iowa-wolves-nba-g-league-lindell-wigginton-keita-bates-diop-minnesota-timberwolves/2519525001/ |access-date=November 26, 2019 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=November 7, 2019}} Battle averaged 8.0 points and 3.5 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Burrows |first1=Ben |title=Was leaving early the right choice for Tyus Battle? Syracuse basketball overseas and in the NBA G League |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2020/03/was-leaving-early-the-right-choice-for-tyus-battle-syracuse-basketball-overseas-and-in-the-nba-g-league.html |access-date=June 16, 2020 |work=[[The Post-Standard]] |date=March 6, 2020}} On July 27, 2020, he signed with [[BC Enisey]] of the [[VTB United League]].{{cite news |title=Enisey Krasnoyarsk signs Tyus Battle |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/enisey-krasnoyarsk-signs-tyus-battle/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 27, 2020 |date=July 27, 2020}} Battle won the VTB United League Slam Dunk Contest during their All-Star Weekend on February 14, 2021.{{cite magazine |title=Tyus Battle Wins VTB United League Slam Dunk Contest |url=https://www.si.com/college/syracuse/basketball/tyus-battle-slam-dunk-contest-vtb-united |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=February 14, 2021}} On July 9, 2021, he has signed with [[Dinamo Sassari]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/banco-di-sardegna-announces-tyus-battle/|title=Banco di Sardegna announces Tyus Battle|last=Maggi|first=Alessandro|date=July 9, 2021|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 9, 2021}} He averaged 7.6 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 1.3 assists per game. On January 11, 2022, Battle signed with [[Hapoel Gilboa Galil]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]].{{cite web |last1=Dahan |first1=Netanel |title=H.Galil Gilboa tabs Tyus Battle, ex Sassari |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/news/726230/H.Galil-Gilboa-tabs-Tyus-Battle,-ex-Sassari |website=Eurobasket |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=January 11, 2022}} On March 20, 2023, he signed with [[ADA Blois Basket 41|ADA Blois]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/France/news/799682/Blois-sign-Tyus-Battle,-ex-H.Gilboa-Galil|title=Blois sign Tyus Battle, ex H.Gilboa Galil|last=|first=|date=March 20, 2023|website=|publisher=Eurobasket|language=En|access-date=March 21, 2023}} ==National team career== In 2013, Battle was cut early in the process of determining the United States team for the 2013 [[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship]]. However, he was one of three players selected to the 12-man team for the [[2014 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] that had not been named to Team USA the year before.{{cite
